questions.name: Eyes: construct an eye on XY
questions.q_figure: A horizontal line segment with its two ends labelled X and Y.
questions.s_figure: The segment XY with equal arcs from X and from Y meeting at A above it and at B below it, the lower arc drawn from centre A through X and Y and the upper arc drawn from centre B through X and Y, making the eye.

questions.name: Perpendicular Bisector: points equally far from X and Y
questions.s_figure: A segment XY with its perpendicular bisector AB crossing it at the midpoint O, and a point P marked on the line AB with PX and PY joined.
A segment XY with arcs of one radius from X and Y meeting at A above it, arcs of a different radius from X and Y meeting at B below it, and the line AB crossing XY at its midpoint at a right angle.
A segment XY with two pairs of arcs of different radii, both pairs above XY, meeting at A and at P, and the line through A and P crossing XY at its midpoint at a right angle.
A segment XY with an arc of one radius from X and an arc of a different radius from Y meeting at a point P that is not on the perpendicular bisector of XY.

questions.name: Right Angle at a Point: construct 90° at O
questions.s_figure: A horizontal line with a point O marked on it, equal arcs from O cutting the line at X and at Y, equal arcs from X and from Y meeting at A above the line, and OA drawn at a right angle to the line.
Four angles of different sizes, each with an arc from its vertex cutting both arms, equal arcs from those two points meeting inside the angle, and the bisector drawn through the vertex.

questions.q_figure: An angle XOY with points B on the upper arm OX and A on the arm OY at equal distances from O, and two equal arcs from A and B meeting at a point C on the far side of O, outside the angle.
questions.s_figure: The same figure with the line CO extended beyond O to a point D inside the angle, bisecting it.

questions.q_figure: A square with four petals inside it, each petal running from the centre of the square to one corner and bounded by curved arcs.
questions.s_figure: The square with the midpoint of each side marked, a semicircle drawn inside the square from each midpoint, and the four petals where the semicircles overlap.

questions.name: Copying an Angle: copy an angle with a compass
questions.q_figure: An angle with vertex A, one arm horizontal and the other slanting up to the right, and a separate horizontal ray starting at a point X.
questions.s_figure: The angle at A with an arc cutting its arms at B and C, an arc of the same radius from X cutting the ray at Z, the length BC marked off from Z to give Y, and the ray XY making the same angle as at A.

questions.q_figure: Four angles of different sizes drawn in different orientations on the page.
questions.s_figure: Each of the four angles drawn beside its copy, with the arcs and the transferred length shown.
A line m and a point B off it, a line l through B cutting m at A, the angle between l and m at A copied at B with equal arcs, and the line n through B parallel to m.

questions.name: Angles Round a Point: the gap and the 70° angle
questions.q_figure: Six triangular pieces fanned round a point O with angles 40°, 60°, 50°, 30°, 40° and 90° at O, leaving a gap marked ∠AOI with a question mark, and a separate triangular piece with a 70° angle beside the figure.
questions.s_figure: The same fan with the gap labelled 50° and the 70° piece shown too wide to fit it.

questions.name: Hexagon from Triangles: AOD, BOE and COF are straight lines
questions.q_figure: A regular hexagon ABCDEF with its centre O joined to all six corners, making six equal triangles.
questions.s_figure: The same hexagon with the three lines AOD, BOE and COF drawn through O and the three 60° angles on each side of O marked.

questions.name: Regular Hexagon: side 4 cm
questions.s_figure: A circle of radius 4 cm with its centre O, six points marked round it by stepping an arc of radius 4 cm from one point to the next, and the six points joined in order to make a regular hexagon.

questions.name: 60° Angle: construct it and say why
questions.s_figure: A segment AX with an arc from A cutting it at B, an arc of the same radius from B cutting the first arc at C, and AC and BC drawn, making the equilateral triangle ABC with ∠CAX = 60°.

questions.name: Regular Hexagon: side 5 cm
questions.s_figure: A regular hexagon ABCDEF with every side 5 cm, drawn by building a 120° angle with arcs at each corner.

questions.name: Related Constructions: 30° and 15° angles
questions.s_figure: A line with a point A on it, a 60° angle at A made with equal arcs, its bisector giving 30°, and the bisector of that 30° angle giving 15°.

questions.name: 6-Pointed Star: the six point triangles
questions.q_figure: A six-pointed star with its outer points labelled A, B, C, D, E, F and its six inner corners labelled G, H, I, J, K, L, forming a hexagon in the middle.
questions.s_figure: The same star with a 120° angle marked at each inner corner of the hexagon and a 60° angle marked at the base of each outer point.
A line l with a point P above it, an arc from P cutting l at X and Y, equal arcs from X and Y below l meeting at Q, and the line PQ meeting l at O at a right angle.

questions.name: Tiling Grids: a 4 × 6 grid
questions.q_figure: A rectangular grid of unit squares with 4 rows and 6 columns, and beside it a vertical 2 × 1 tile and a horizontal 2 × 1 tile.
questions.s_figure: The 4 by 6 grid covered by 12 vertical 2 × 1 tiles, two in each of the six columns.

questions.name: Tiling Grids: a 4 × 7 grid
questions.q_figure: A rectangular grid of unit squares with 4 rows and 7 columns, and beside it a 2 × 1 tile.
questions.s_figure: The 4 by 7 grid covered by 14 vertical 2 × 1 tiles, two in each of the seven columns.

questions.name: Tiling Grids: why 5 × 7 cannot be tiled
questions.q_figure: A rectangular grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 7 columns, and beside it a 2 × 1 tile.

questions.name: Tiling m × n Grids: both even
questions.s_figure: A grid with 6 rows and 4 columns with three vertical 2 × 1 tiles stacked in every column.

questions.name: Tiling m × n Grids: one even, one odd
questions.s_figure: A grid with 3 rows and 4 columns with two horizontal 2 × 1 tiles in every row.

questions.name: Tiling m × n Grids: both odd
Missing Squares: top right of a 5 × 3 grid
questions.q_figure: A grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 3 columns in which the top right square is missing.
questions.s_figure: The same region covered by one horizontal 2 × 1 tile in the top row and six vertical tiles below it.

questions.name: Missing Squares: middle of the second row
questions.q_figure: A grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 3 columns in which the middle square of the second row is missing.
questions.s_figure: The same region covered by seven 2 × 1 tiles: horizontal tiles in the top row's left two squares and in the right two squares of row 3, vertical tiles in the right column of rows 1 and 2, the left column of rows 2 and 3 and each column of rows 4 and 5.

questions.name: Colouring Squares: top middle removed
questions.q_figure: A grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 3 columns in which the middle square of the top row is missing.
questions.s_figure: The same region coloured like a chessboard with white corners, showing 8 white squares and 6 black squares.

questions.name: Colouring Squares: another square to remove
questions.q_figure: A grid of unit squares with 5 rows and 3 columns coloured like a chessboard with white corners.
questions.s_figure: The same grid with its seven black squares marked: the top middle square and the squares in row 2 column 1, row 2 column 3, row 3 column 2, row 4 column 1, row 4 column 3 and row 5 column 2.

questions.q_figure: A region of 12 unit squares in which the top two rows have 2 squares each at the left and the bottom two rows have 4 squares each, and beside it an L-shaped tile made of 3 unit squares.
questions.s_figure: The region covered by four L-shaped tiles of 3 squares each, turned to different positions.

questions.q_figure: An 8 by 8 grid of unit squares with the top right corner square and the bottom left corner square missing, and beside it a 2 × 1 tile.
questions.s_figure: The same region coloured like a chessboard, with the two missing corners the same colour, leaving 32 squares of one colour and 30 of the other.
